- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.5), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 to counteract pessimism.  
- Model consistently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon after sharp price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by lowering forecast 0.5–1.0 for the first 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias: over-forecasting after strong upward moves, under-forecasting after strong downward moves — adjust by adding 0.3–0.7 to forecast if recent price moved >1.5% in 3 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the final 5–7 days; apply a “tail correction” by adding 0.2–0.5 to the last 5–7 forecasted values if sentiment remains positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.5 → +0.8), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 0.3–0.6 ahead of the sentiment shift.
